clue.text: Complained vehicle went too fast, cutting dangerous bend

parts.note: a car is a common vehicle

indicators.note: cutting tells us to remove something from the word before it

parts.note: sped means drove too fast
an S-bend is a sharp double bend in a road, so the letter S stands for it

explanation.surface: A driver complains after a car took a hazardous corner at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: An S-bend is a road-sign hazard; 'cutting' here means removing, not driving across the corner.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault or grumble, so carped is a past-tense synonym for complained.

clue.text: A letter read out in confession

indicators.note: read out means the words are spoken, so we want something sounding the same

parts.note: a vowel is a kind of letter, so the phrase gives a plus vowel

explanation.surface: A single letter is read aloud in the confessional.
explanation.walkthrough: A VOWEL said aloud sounds like AVOWAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open admission or declaration, a confession of something.

clue.text: After short walk, imagined being given sustenance

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, losing the last letter

parts.note: prom, short for promenade, is a walk
to vision something is to imagine it

explanation.surface: After a brief stroll, someone dreamed of being fed.
explanation.walkthrough: PROM loses its M to give PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: To be provisioned is to be supplied with food and stores, so being given sustenance.

clue.text: Mime, perhaps, being performed in Scottish town

parts.note: mime is an example of silent or dumb art
a show that is on is being performed

explanation.surface: A mime act is staged in a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals that mime is an example of DUMB ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbarton is a town on the Clyde in west-central Scotland.

clue.text: Island's main road dividing two preserves

indicators.note: dividing means the road sits between the two preserves, splitting them

parts.note: jam is one preserve
can is a verb meaning to preserve food, here a second preserve
the A1 is Britain's longest main road, written AI with the figure as a letter I

explanation.surface: A Caribbean main road runs between two fruit preserve factories.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; the figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something belonging to the Caribbean island of Jamaica, matching the possessive form.

clue.text: Caretaker picked up rubbish after bank holiday

indicators.note: after puts the rubbish piece behind the holiday

parts.note: January 1st, New Year's Day, is a bank holiday, written JAN I

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted, read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A school caretaker gathers litter after the holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reads upward in this down entry; New Year's Day, 1 January, is a UK bank holiday, its figure written as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor looks after a building, so it is a caretaker.

clue.text: Officer course for American students

definitions.meaning: an army officer ranking above captain
a US student's main subject of study at college

explanation.definitionFit: Major is both a military rank and, in US colleges, the main field of a student's degree.

clue.text: A bit of tonsillitis could you make this

definitions.text: A bit of tonsillitis could you make this

indicators.note: a bit of means just part of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A sore throat might leave you feeling poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside tonsILLitis, and the whole clue also describes the effect of the infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonsillitis is an infection that makes one unwell, so this word for sick fits the whole clue.

clue.text: Count on these charges to trap clever man, caught only once

indicators.note: to trap means to enclose, so the graduate letters go inside
only once means one of the two C letters is dropped

parts.note: accuses means charges with an offence
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate and so a clever man

explanation.surface: Prosecutors bring charges to snare a smart man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only once' keeps a single C of the two; BA, a degree, is the crossword's usual clever man.
explanation.definitionFit: Abacuses are counting frames with beads, so you count on them.

clue.text: Heart of Exmoor, endless bother for drivers

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters, here the middle two of Exmoor
endless says to drop the final letter of the synonym for bother

parts.note: torment means to bother or harass

explanation.surface: Something in the middle of the moorland keeps troubling motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: Exmoor is a moorland national park in south-west England. 'endless' chops the T from TORMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Motormen are drivers of trams, trains or other motor vehicles.

clue.text: Prison's no good, the reverse of secure for this fellow

indicators.note: no good means the letter G, standing for good, is taken away

parts.note: jug is slang for prison

indicators.note: the reverse of says to read the synonym for secure backwards

parts.note: to nail something is to secure it

explanation.surface: A man in jail finds his prison is useless, the opposite of secure.
explanation.walkthrough: JUG loses G to give JU; 'the reverse of' turns NAIL into LIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Julian is a man's given name, so it names a particular fellow.

clue.text: Pretentious daughter getting into "opera on line'

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another means it is placed after it
getting into means the letter for daughter goes inside the rest

parts.note: Aida is Verdi's opera
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A snobbish girl joins in a performance of opera broadcast online.
explanation.walkthrough: AIDA placed after L gives LAIDA, and D goes in after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da is an informal adjective for affected or pretentious manners or speech.

clue.text: They're oddly lacking a boundary

indicators.note: oddly picks out the letters in the odd-numbered positions

parts.note: minus means without or lacking

explanation.surface: Some peculiar people have no sense of limits.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of THEYRE are T, E, R.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is an end point or limit, and Terminus was the Roman god of boundaries.

clue.text: Trouble with vermin in empty farmhouse, creature's natural habitat

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word is removed, keeping first and last letters

parts.note: in biology a station is the place where a plant or animal naturally lives

explanation.surface: An abandoned farmhouse has become the natural home of pests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves F and E of farmhouse. STATION in its ecological sense is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: An infestation is an invasion by pests or vermin, a trouble with them.

clue.text: Appealing to no-one for such a loan?

definitions.text: Appealing to no-one for such a loan?

parts.words: Appealing to no-one for such a loan?
parts.note: a loan carrying no charge is described by a phrase that could also mean holding no attraction for anyone at all

explanation.surface: A lender wonders which kind of loan nobody would find attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan with no charge on the borrowed money is the plain sense, the joke being 'free of interest' as dull.

clue.text: I attend sporting event weekly

definitions.meaning: one who watches a game or match
the name of a long-running British weekly magazine

explanation.definitionFit: A spectator watches an event, and The Spectator is a British weekly political magazine.

clue.text: Repair finished on country house, say

parts.note: over means ended or finished

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, so we want a word sounding the same

parts.note: a hall is a large country house

explanation.surface: A country mansion needs repair once building work is done.
explanation.walkthrough: HALL said aloud sounds like HAUL.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul a machine is to examine and repair it thoroughly.

clue.text: Fashion designer's clothing cleric in formal attire

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping round, so the rearranged letters surround the cleric
to fashion is to shape anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A couturier dresses a clergyman in smart clothes for a formal event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' rearranges the designer's letters to EINGDRESS; 'clothing' wraps that round the archdeacon's title after its first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening dress is the formal clothing worn to grand occasions at night, so it is formal attire.

clue.text: Criminal sort captured by commander and put to death

indicators.note: captured by means held inside the next piece

parts.note: a dey was the title of the Ottoman governor of Algiers, a commander

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain is caught by the commanding officer and executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' reorders the four letters to make STRO; 'captured by' holds them inside the Algerian ruler's title.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy an animal is to kill it, so the sense put to death fits.

clue.text: Family in which the females stay young, presumably

definitions.text: Family in which the females stay young, presumably

parts.words: Family in which the females stay young, presumably
parts.note: a household split into two words describes one where only the males grow older

explanation.surface: A household in which women never seem to grow older.
explanation.definitionFit: A ménage is a household, the people living together as a family.

clue.text: Dry quality of canned sardines

indicators.note: canned fish are packed tightly, suggesting the letters are jumbled up together

explanation.surface: Tinned sardines can taste rather dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Aridness is the state of being parched, so it is a quality of dryness.

clue.text: Boat crew worried, according to radio

indicators.note: according to radio means heard over the air, so spoken

parts.note: ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

explanation.surface: Rowers were anxious about what the radio reported.
explanation.walkthrough: ATE said aloud sounds like the rowing word.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight is a racing rowing boat with eight oarsmen, or its crew.

clue.text: Nobleman heading for this island

parts.note: a thane was a Scottish or Anglo-Saxon nobleman

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A lord sets course for an island.
explanation.walkthrough: THANET is in Kent, at England's south-east corner; once cut off by a channel, it is still called the Isle of Thanet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Thanet is a historic island, now joined to the mainland, in north-east Kent.

clue.text: Sack of newspapers for collection

indicators.note: a sack of something is that thing's bag, so the newspaper word comes first

parts.note: rag is a scornful word for a newspaper
a sack is a bag

explanation.surface: A bag full of old papers is gathered for recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Sack of newspapers' as a rag bag, a bag for rags.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragbag is a miscellaneous jumble, a mixed collection of odds and ends.

clue.text: Entomologist's enthusiasm

definitions.meaning: what an insect scientist studies, an insect

explanation.definitionFit: An entomologist studies insects, informally called by this word, which also means a craze.

clue.text: Writer produces article on Pied Piper's mission, putting name at the end

indicators.note: putting names the moving of one letter to a new spot
at the end says where the moved letter goes: last
in an across clue, one thing on another means it follows it

parts.note: the Pied Piper of Hamelin was hired to rid the town of rats, so his task was catching rats
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An author writes an article about the Pied Piper ridding Hamelin of rats.
explanation.walkthrough: RATTING then A gives RATTINGA; 'putting' the N 'at the end' makes the playwright Terence RATTIGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence Rattigan was an English playwright, author of The Winslow Boy, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Clever, closing window a little bit

indicators.note: closing means shutting round, so the word for clever surrounds the other

parts.note: sly means cunning or clever
a light is a window or pane

explanation.surface: A smart person shuts the window just a fraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closing' looks like shutting the window, but it means the clever word closes round the window word.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly is an adverb meaning to a small degree, matching the adverbial phrase.

clue.text: Commissioned officer, one giving order

definitions.meaning: an officer who has risen from the ranks to be commissioned
someone who ranks things puts them into an order

explanation.definitionFit: A ranker is both an officer promoted from the rank and file and literally one who ranks or sorts.
